newsitem.title: UK: IBCA says cuts Sainsbury l-term rating.
newsitem.headline: IBCA says cuts Sainsbury l-term rating.

text.p: IBCA, the European credit rating agency said on Thursday it lowered its long-term rating for J Sainsbury Plc to AA minus from AA.
The agency also said it maintained its short-term rating at A1 plus.

IBCA said the core Sainsbury's UK food retail chain, accounted for about 81 percent of group turnover of 12.6 billion stg and 91 percent of group operating profit (before exceptionals) of 854 million stg in fiscal year 1996.

"(It) has underperformed the UK food retail market during the last 18 months," IBCA said in a statement."Like-for-like sales of 2.6 percent in fiscal year 1996 were below the 6 percent average achieved by the UK majors."
It said this was also significantly below the rates seen at the retailer's two principal rivals, Tesco at about 9.0 percent and Asda at about 12 percent.

"Tesco's acquisition of William Low and higher sales growth means that Sainsbury's market share of 12.5 percent now lies second behind Tesco (13.9 percent) in what remains a highly competitive operating environment," IBCA said.
It said operating cash flow remained strong, reflecting the cash generative nature of food retailing and Sainsbury's high net margins.
However, gearing has increased and a small cash outflow in fiscal year 1997 was expected to raise net gearing slightly above the fiscal year end 1996 level of 3 percent, the rating agency said.

It said Sainsbury's principal problem has been the ineffective communication of the value of its offer. The Reward Card loyalty scheme, the introduction of Extra Reward Points on certain products, the re-launch and extension of the group's Economy range and an ongoing programme to improve the quality of both products and customer service underline the group's attempts to regain some of the lost ground.

Gross margins are expected to fall further in fiscal 1997 due to the cost of a fierce price petrol price war, combined with the costs of the loyalty scheme, although the retailer is keen to boost volumes without margin dilution, IBCA said.

IBCA noted that expansion and store extensions within the core chain will continue, while the conversion of the acquired Texas DIY stores to the more successful Homebase store format will be accelerated.
All DIY stores are to be rebadged as Homebase by the start of December 1996 and conversion will be phased in over the next two to three years, IBCA said.

In the US, Shaw's opening programme will quicken through new openings and small bolt-on acquisitions. Sainsbury's will not increase its stake in Giant above 20 percent, but acquisition of full control should not be ruled out in the medium term.
